facts.note: https://www.michigan.gov/lara/bureau-list/bcc/sections/licensing-section/exam-lic/mechanical-examination-licensing-registration-application-information ; https://www.michigan.gov/-/media/Project/Websites/lara/Folder14/NOTICE_for_web_NewMechanicalLegislationAmending407Art8.pdf

facts.source: Minn. Stat. §326B.805; Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry (DLI)
facts.fact: The Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry licenses residential building contractors, residential remodelers, and residential roofers; the state statute covers residential work only. Someone who does only licensable specialty work and expects $15,000 or less in gross annual receipts can get a certificate of exemption instead of a license.
facts.note: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326B.805

facts.source: Minn. Stat. §326B.83 subd. 3; DLI Residential Building Contractor exam guide and exam page
facts.fact: Each Minnesota residential license must have a qualifying person who passes a written exam on technical knowledge, business management, and state law. DLI gives the residential building contractor exam itself at its St. Paul office and outstate locations: 110 multiple-choice questions in 5.5 hours, 70% to pass, with DLI providing the statutes and code references and a desktop calculator.
facts.note: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326B.83 ; https://dli.mn.gov/node/2696 ; https://www.dli.mn.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/exam_guide.pdf (the guide's outline also mentions '60 scored questions', so not every item may count)

facts.fact: Minnesota residential licensees must carry commercial general liability insurance of at least $100,000 per occurrence and $300,000 aggregate for bodily injury plus $25,000 property damage, or a single-limit policy of $300,000 per occurrence and aggregate. Licensed residential roofers must also post a bond of at least $15,000, and manufactured home installers a bond of at least $2,500.
facts.note: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326B.86

facts.source: Minn. Stat. §326B.821; DLI residential contractor exam page
facts.fact: A Minnesota residential contractor license renews every two years. To renew, the qualifying person must complete 14 hours of approved continuing education.
facts.note: https://dli.mn.gov/node/2696

facts.fact: Minnesota licenses electricians statewide. A Class A journeyworker electrician needs at least four years of experience acceptable to the commissioner (one year of credit is possible for an approved two-year electrical program), and a Class A master needs one year as a licensed journeyworker, five years of experience, or a four-year electrical degree. Other licenses include installers, power limited technicians, and Class A and B electrical contractors.
facts.note: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326B.33

facts.fact: Minnesota requires licenses for master, restricted master, journeyworker, and restricted journeyworker plumbers, plus a separate contractor license for anyone offering plumbing work. A plumbing contractor's responsible individual must be a master plumber, and the contractor needs a $25,000 bond, liability insurance of at least $50,000 per person and $100,000 per occurrence, and $10,000 property damage coverage.
facts.note: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326B.46

facts.fact: A Minnesota contractor dealing directly with the owner must include the statutory prelien notice in the written contract, or deliver it within 10 days after the work is agreed upon if there is no written contract. Subcontractors and suppliers must deliver it personally or by certified mail within 45 days after first furnishing. The notice is not required for residential projects over four units or for most nonresidential projects over 5,000 usable square feet.
facts.note: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/514.011

facts.fact: A Minnesota mechanics' lien statement must be recorded with the county recorder (or registrar of titles) and served on the owner within 120 days after the claimant's last work or materials. A foreclosure action must be started within one year after the date of the last item listed in the recorded lien statement.
facts.note: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/514.08 ; https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/514.12

facts.source: Mississippi State Board of Contractors (MSBOC), Frequently Asked Questions
facts.fact: The Mississippi State Board of Contractors (MSBOC) requires a commercial license for contractors and subcontractors on commercial projects over $50,000, including equipment installation. Fire sprinkler work needs a commercial license on public projects over $5,000 and private projects over $10,000.
facts.note: https://www.msboc.us/general-info/frequently-asked-questions/

facts.fact: MSBOC requires a residential license for new residential construction over $50,000 and for residential remodeling, additions, or roofing over $10,000. Electrical, mechanical/HVAC, and plumbing subcontractors on residential construction or improvement projects must also hold an MSBOC license, and the FAQ lists no minimum dollar threshold for them.
facts.note: https://www.msboc.us/general-info/frequently-asked-questions/

facts.source: MSBOC Testing page; MSBOC Licenses page
facts.fact: Every MSBOC license applicant must pass the Mississippi Law and Business Management exam, plus a trade exam when the classification calls for one (some specialty classifications have none). All exams are open book and given by PSI. NASCLA Accredited Exams (Commercial General Building and Master Electrical) are accepted as optional alternatives for those trade exams.
facts.note: https://www.msboc.us/general-info/testing/ ; https://www.msboc.us/contractors/licenses/ ; question counts and passing scores are in the PSI bulletin, not checked here

facts.fact: A Mississippi commercial license applicant must submit a CPA-reviewed financial statement showing net worth of $50,000 or more for a major classification, or $20,000 or more for a specialty classification. Residential applicants have no net worth requirement on this page.
facts.note: https://www.msboc.us/contractors/licenses/

facts.fact: Every Mississippi license applicant and renewal must show proof of general liability insurance. Commercial licensees need at least $300,000 per occurrence and $600,000 aggregate with MSBOC listed on the policy, while residential licensees have no minimum amount. Workers' compensation is required once a business has 5 or more employees.
facts.note: https://www.msboc.us/contractors/licenses/ ; https://www.msboc.us/general-info/frequently-asked-questions/ (the Licenses page says 'per occurrence or $600,000 aggregate', the FAQ says 'and')

facts.source: MSBOC FAQ; MSBOC Continuing Education page
facts.fact: Mississippi commercial and residential licenses are valid for one year and renew annually; a license can be renewed up to 180 days after it expires, and after that a new application is required. Each qualifying party on a residential license issued on or after July 1, 2015 must complete 2 credit hours of continuing education from a board-approved provider.
facts.note: https://www.msboc.us/general-info/frequently-asked-questions/ ; https://www.msboc.us/contractors/continuing-education/ (the CE page does not say how often the 2 hours are due)

facts.fact: Mississippi reciprocity agreements waive only the trade exam, so every applicant must still pass the Mississippi Business and Law exam. Agreements exist with boards in states including Alabama, Arkansas, California, Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, and Tennessee. Mississippi no longer has a reciprocity agreement with Louisiana but still accepts passing Louisiana exam scores.
facts.note: https://www.msboc.us/contractors/reciprocity/

facts.source: Miss. Code §§85-7-405 and 85-7-421 (summary by Baker Donelson of SB 2622, 2014)
facts.fact: A Mississippi construction lien must be recorded with the chancery clerk in the county where the property is located within 90 days after the claimant's last work or materials. The lien is void unless a payment action is filed within 180 days after the lien is filed.
facts.note: Taken from a law-firm summary of the 2014 lien law rewrite (https://bakerdonelson.com/summary-of-senate-bill-2622---mississippis-construction-lien-law-03-26-2014); the official statute text was not reached.

facts.fact: On Mississippi projects other than single-family residential construction, a claimant who has no contract with the general contractor (or with the owner, if there is no contractor) must give the contractor (or owner) written pre-lien notice within 30 days after first delivering labor, services or materials, or it forfeits its lien right. On single-family residential projects, a subcontractor, supplier or design professional with no contract with the owner must give the owner a pre-lien notice at least 10 days before filing a lien, and the owner's payments to the contractor made before receiving that notice are a defense.
facts.note: https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-85/chapter-7/article-21/section-85-7-407/ ; https://law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/title-85/chapter-7/article-21/section-85-7-409/
facts.reviewed: Checked Miss. Code 85-7-407 and 85-7-409 (2025 code via Justia). The 30-day notice goes to the contractor (or the owner if there is no contractor), comes from claimants with no privity with the contractor, and applies to every project except single-family residential (so multifamily is covered too, not just 'non-residential'). Missing the notice forfeits the lien.

facts.source: Secondary licensing guides (no state GC licensing statute found)
facts.fact: Missouri has no statewide license for general or building contractors. Licensing is handled locally, so requirements vary by city and county (for example Kansas City, St. Louis County, and Springfield), and contractors must check each jurisdiction where they work.
facts.note: Widely reported on secondary sites (e.g., adaptdigitalsolutions.com); no official state page stating 'no license' was found. The Missouri Division of Professional Registration licenses no general contractors.

facts.fact: Missouri has no statewide plumber or HVAC license. Plumbing and mechanical licenses (master, journeyman, contractor) are issued by local jurisdictions such as Kansas City, St. Louis City, and St. Louis County.
facts.note: Based on secondary sources; confirm with local jurisdictions. Electrical is the only trade with a (voluntary) statewide contractor license.

facts.source: RSMo 324.900-324.945; Missouri Office of Statewide Electrical Contractors FAQ; Missouri House bill summary SB 862 (2018)
facts.fact: Missouri offers an optional statewide electrical contractor license through the Office of Statewide Electrical Contractors in the Division of Professional Registration. A statewide license holder may do electrical contracting in any political subdivision, and localities cannot make that holder get a local license requiring another exam. Contractors working only where they hold a local license, or where none is required, do not need the statewide license.
facts.note: https://pr.mo.gov/electricalcontractors-FAQ-Contractors.asp (FAQ dated 2017) ; https://documents.house.mo.gov/billtracking/bills181/sumpdf/SB0862t.pdf

facts.fact: A Missouri statewide electrical contractor applicant must pass an approved National Electrical Code-based exam from an independent testing agency and carry at least $500,000 in liability insurance. Experience can be 12,000 hours of installation, 10,000 hours plus a DOL-approved journeyman certificate, 8,000 hours plus an accredited associate degree, 4,000 supervisory hours plus a four-year electrical engineering degree, or a local contractor or master license held six of the past eight years. Licenses renew every three years by September 30.
facts.note: https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/AdRules/csr/current/20csr/20c2117-2.pdf

facts.fact: A Missouri original contractor must give the owner a written notice, in the statutory 10-point bold language, before receiving any payment. It can be delivered at contract signing, when materials are delivered, when work starts, or with the first invoice, and giving it is a condition for the original contractor to have any valid mechanic's lien.
facts.note: https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=429.012

facts.fact: In Missouri, a mechanic's lien statement must be filed within six months after the debt accrues (60 days after removal for rental equipment). Anyone other than the original contractor must give the owner 10 days' notice before filing the lien, stating the amount and from whom it is owed.
facts.note: https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=429.080 ; https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=429.100

facts.fact: A suit to enforce a Missouri mechanic's lien must be started within six months after the lien is filed, or the lien ceases to exist.
facts.note: https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=429.170

facts.source: Montana Department of Labor and Industry (DLI), Construction Contractor License (CCL) Program; HB 239 (2025); MCA Title 37, ch. 45
facts.fact: Starting January 1, 2026, Montana's construction contractor registration became a Construction Contractor License (CCL) administered by the Department of Labor and Industry under HB 239 (2025). Existing registrations converted automatically and kept their expiration dates. The department enforces conduct such as fraud and misrepresentation, not workmanship quality.
facts.note: https://boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/construction-contractor/ ; https://erd.dli.mt.gov/_docs/work-comp-regs/HB-239-Notice-to-Construction-Contractors.pdf

facts.source: DLI HB 239 Notice to Construction Contractors; DLI CCL Program page; MCA 39-9-211
facts.fact: Montana construction contractors with employees must hold the CCL. Independent contractors with no employees are exempt from the license, as are the other exemptions listed in MCA 39-9-211. Anyone hiring multiple trades on a single job or permit for their own property also counts as a construction contractor.
facts.note: https://erd.dli.mt.gov/_docs/work-comp-regs/HB-239-Notice-to-Construction-Contractors.pdf ; https://boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/construction-contractor/

facts.source: MCA 37-68-304 and 37-68-305; Montana State Electrical Board
facts.fact: The Montana State Electrical Board licenses master, journeyman, and residential electricians as well as electrical contractors. A journeyman needs 8,000 hours of practical experience and a residential electrician needs 4,000 hours in residential construction of fewer than five units, or either can complete an approved apprenticeship. A master needs 8,000 hours of journeyman-level experience, or an electrical engineering degree plus 2,000 hours of practical experience.
facts.note: https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0370/chapter_0680/part_0030/section_0050/0370-0680-0030-0050.html ; https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0370/chapter_0680/part_0030/section_0040/0370-0680-0030-0040.html

facts.fact: Montana electrical licensees must complete 16 hours of continuing education as outlined in ARM 24.225.2102 to renew.
facts.note: https://boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/electrical/

facts.source: MCA 37-69-304; Montana Board of Plumbers; ARM 24.180.2102
facts.fact: The Montana Board of Plumbers licenses journeyman and master plumbers. A journeyman needs a record of 5 years of legally obtained plumbing experience or an approved apprenticeship, must pass a written exam, and may work only while employed by a licensed master plumber. Plumbing licensees complete 4 hours of continuing education each renewal cycle.
facts.note: https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0370/chapter_0690/part_0030/section_0040/0370-0690-0030-0040.html ; https://boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/plumbers/

facts.fact: In Montana, a lien claimant who did not contract directly with the owner must give the contracting owner a notice of right to claim a lien within 20 days after first furnishing services or materials (45 days in certain lender-funded projects that are not owner-occupied homes). A late notice limits the lien to work furnished in the 20 days before it was given, and the notice is not required for original contractors, wage earners, dwellings for five or more families, or commercial improvements.
facts.note: https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0710/chapter_0030/part_0050/section_0310/0710-0030-0050-0310.html
keywords: Montana notice of right to claim lien

facts.fact: A Montana construction lien must be filed no later than 90 days after the claimant's final furnishing of services or materials, or after the owner files a notice of completion. A foreclosure action must be started within 2 years after the lien is filed.
facts.note: https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0710/chapter_0030/part_0050/section_0350/0710-0030-0050-0350.html ; https://mca.legmt.gov/bills/mca/title_0710/chapter_0030/part_0050/section_0620/0710-0030-0050-0620.html

facts.fact: Montana has no statewide HVAC or mechanical contractor license; HVAC businesses with employees hold the general Construction Contractor License, and some cities add local requirements.
facts.note: No official state page confirming the absence of an HVAC license was found; based on secondary sources.

facts.source: Nebraska Department of Labor, Contractor Registration; Nebraska Contractor Registration Act (Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-2101 et seq.)
facts.fact: Nebraska has no statewide general contractor license or exam. Instead, every contractor doing business in Nebraska must register with the Nebraska Department of Labor, and the department notes that registration does not ensure quality of work or protect against fraud. Registration carries an annual fee and is renewed online.
facts.note: https://dol.nebraska.gov/LaborStandards/Contractors

facts.source: Nebraska Department of Labor, Contractor Registration
facts.fact: Nebraska contractors with one or more employees must file a current workers' compensation certificate of insurance (ACORD 25) to register. A contractor whose workers' compensation coverage expires is removed from the list of registered contractors.
facts.note: https://dol.nebraska.gov/LaborStandards/Contractors

facts.source: Nebraska State Electrical Division / State Electrical Board; Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-2101 et seq.
facts.fact: Nebraska licenses electricians statewide through the State Electrical Division. License types include apprentice electrician, journeyman electrician, residential journeyman wireman, electrical contractor, and fire alarm installer, and the state has no separate master electrician license. Exams are given through PSI.
facts.note: https://electrical.nebraska.gov/

facts.fact: Nebraska electrical licensees must complete 12 contact hours of continuing education by January 1 of each odd-numbered year. At least 6 of those hours must cover the National Electrical Code.
facts.note: https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=81-2117.01

facts.fact: Nebraska has no statewide plumbing or HVAC license; plumbers and mechanical contractors are licensed by cities such as Omaha and Lincoln.
facts.note: Based on secondary sources; no official state page confirming the absence of a plumbing license was found.

facts.source: Nebraska Construction Lien Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. 52-137 and 52-140
facts.fact: Under the Nebraska Construction Lien Act, a lien must be recorded no later than 120 days after the claimant's final furnishing of services or materials. A recorded lien stays enforceable for two years, but if an interested party makes a written demand, the claimant has 30 days to file suit (or record an affidavit that the contract price is not yet due) or the lien lapses.
facts.note: https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=52-137 ; https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=52-140

facts.fact: A Nebraska lien claimant must send the contracting owner a copy of the recorded lien within 10 days after recording. When the owner is a protected party, a claimant who did not contract directly with the owner may give a notice of the right to assert a lien, and the owner's good-faith payments made before receiving that notice or a recorded lien reduce what the claimant can recover.
facts.note: https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=52-135 ; https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=52-136 ('protected party' is defined elsewhere in the Act, generally an owner of residential property)
keywords: Nebraska notice of right to assert lien

facts.source: Nevada State Contractors Board (NSCB); NRS 624.215; NSCB License Classifications page
facts.fact: Nevada contractors are licensed statewide by the Nevada State Contractors Board (NSCB). Licenses fall into Class A (general engineering), Class B (general building, with subclasses such as B-2 residential and small commercial and B-7 residential remodeling), and Class C (specialty trades, with 42 subclassifications including plumbing and electrical).
facts.note: https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-624.html ; https://www.nvcontractorsboard.com/licensing/license-classifications/

facts.fact: Nevada exempts repair or maintenance work valued under $1,000 including labor and materials from licensing, but the exemption does not apply if a building permit is required. It also does not apply to plumbing, electrical, refrigeration, heating, or air-conditioning work, to work in any classification the Board has designated as significantly affecting public health, safety and welfare, or to work that is part of a larger project worth $500 or more (or split into contracts under $500 to evade the law).
facts.note: https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-624.html
facts.reviewed: NRS 624.031(6) has two more exceptions the fact left out: work in any classification the Board has designated as significantly affecting public health, safety and welfare, and work done by a licensee or its employee. A student could rely on the $1,000 exemption for work the Board has excluded.

facts.source: NRS 624.220; NSCB Contractor's License Application page
facts.fact: The NSCB sets a monetary limit on each Nevada license, which is the maximum contract amount the contractor may take on for one client at a single site or subdivision. The type of financial statement an applicant must submit depends on the monetary limit requested.
facts.note: https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-624.html ; https://www.nvcontractorsboard.com/licensing/contractors-license-application/

facts.fact: A Nevada license applicant's trade qualifier must show 4 years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee, or contractor in the trade, gained within the past 15 years and documented with certification forms. Licensure by endorsement is available to those actively licensed for the past 4 years in a state with substantially similar requirements.
facts.note: https://www.nvcontractorsboard.com/licensing/contractors-license-application/

facts.source: NSCB License Examinations page; PSI Nevada 'A' Classification and CMS bulletin (updated 3/25/2026)
facts.fact: Nevada's management qualifier must pass the Contractor Management Survey (CMS) business and law exam from PSI. It is open book using the Construction Business and Law Manual for Nevada and has 60 scored questions (plus 3 unscored) in 120 minutes, with 45 correct (75%) needed to pass. Trade exams are closed book except for code references listed in each content outline.
facts.note: https://www.nvcontractorsboard.com/licensing/license-examinations/ ; https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/291

facts.fact: Nevada candidates get three attempts at an exam; failing a third time voids the application, and the candidate may reapply after 30 days. Nevada may waive the trade exam for applicants who qualify for licensure by endorsement, based on its State Equivalency Chart.
facts.note: https://www.nvcontractorsboard.com/licensing/license-examinations/

facts.fact: Every Nevada contractor must post a license bond of $1,000 to $500,000, with the amount set by the Board at approval based on license type, monetary limit, and the applicant's financial responsibility and experience. Residential pool and spa contractors post a separate consumer bond of $10,000 to $400,000.
facts.note: https://nvcontractorsboard.com/bonds

facts.fact: A Nevada notice of lien must be recorded within 90 days after the latest of completion of the work of improvement, the claimant's last delivery of materials or equipment, or its last performance of work. If the owner records and serves a valid notice of completion, the deadline shrinks to 40 days after that recording. On single-family and multifamily residential projects, claimants other than laborers must also serve a 15-day notice of intent to lien on the owner and prime contractor before recording.
facts.note: https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-108.html

facts.fact: A Nevada mechanics' lien binds the property for only 6 months after the notice of lien is recorded unless a foreclosure action is started within that time. A written, recorded extension can lengthen this, but never beyond 1 year after recording.
facts.note: https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-108.html

facts.fact: In Nevada, a lien claimant other than one who contracted directly with the owner (or a laborer) generally must deliver a notice of right to lien to the owner within 31 days after first furnishing materials or performing work, to preserve its lien rights.
facts.note: The 31-day figure is widely reported but the NRS 108.245 text could not be loaded in this session; confirm deadline and exemptions in the statute.
keywords: Nevada notice of right to lien

facts.source: Secondary licensing guides; NH Office of Professional Licensure and Certification (OPLC) board list
facts.fact: New Hampshire has no statewide license for general or building contractors. Licensing at the state level applies to trades such as electricians, plumbers, and gas fitters, and some towns set their own local requirements.
facts.note: No official statement found; inferred from OPLC licensing only trade boards (electricians, mechanical) and from secondary sources such as adaptdigitalsolutions.com.

facts.source: NH Electricians' Board, Office of Professional Licensure and Certification (OPLC); RSA 319-C
facts.fact: The New Hampshire Electricians' Board, part of the Office of Professional Licensure and Certification (OPLC), licenses apprentice, journeyman, master, and high/medium voltage electricians and issues business entity licenses to corporations, LLCs, and partnerships.
facts.note: https://www.oplc.nh.gov/electricians-board

facts.source: NH Employment Security, Licensed, Certified and Registered Occupations in New Hampshire 2021 (Journeyman Electrician)
facts.fact: A New Hampshire journeyman electrician needs four years (8,000 hours) of practical experience as an apprentice to a licensed electrician plus four years of schooling in electricity (150 hours per year), and must pass a written exam administered by PROV. Journeymen work under the direction of a master electrician.
facts.note: Official state publication but dated 2021 (https://www.nhes.nh.gov/elmi/products/licertocc/documents/electjou.pdf); confirm current requirements with the Electricians' Board. The same document lists reciprocity with Maine, Massachusetts, Vermont and several other states.

facts.source: NH OPLC, Electricians Continuing Education page; Electricians' Board page
facts.fact: New Hampshire master and journeyman electricians must complete 15 hours of code update continuing education, with at least 1 hour on changes to RSA 319-C, the board's rules, and installation concerns. The CE is due within one year after the January 1 following publication of each new NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code) edition.
facts.note: https://oplc.nh.gov/electricians-continuing-education ; the Electricians' Board page phrases it as '15 hours of instruction every year', so confirm how often it applies

facts.source: NH Employment Security, Licensed, Certified and Registered Occupations in New Hampshire 2021 (Master Plumber); RSA 153:27
facts.fact: New Hampshire plumbers are licensed by the Mechanical Safety and Licensing Board under OPLC, which also licenses fuel gas fitters. A master plumber must be at least 18, hold a journeyman plumber license for at least six months, and pass a written exam. Plumbing licenses renew every two years with 6 hours of continuing education per cycle (3 hours per year).
facts.note: Official state publication dated 2021 (https://www.nhes.nh.gov/elmi/products/licertocc/documents/plumbmas.pdf); RSA 153:27 (https://gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/XII/153/153-27.htm) confirms the board and plumber classes but not the experience or CE figures.

facts.source: RSA 447:2, 447:9, 447:10 (summary in ALFA International Construction Compendium)
facts.fact: A New Hampshire mechanic's lien arises automatically for labor or materials worth $15 or more but lasts only 120 days after the services are performed or materials furnished. To keep it, the claimant must sue and secure the lien by a court attachment of the property within that 120-day window.
facts.note: From a law-firm compendium (https://www.alfainternational.com/compendium/construction/new-hampshire/); the official RSA 447 pages on gencourt.state.nh.us were rate-limited (HTTP 429) in this session.

facts.source: RSA 447:5, 447:6, 447:8 (summary in ALFA International Construction Compendium)
facts.fact: In New Hampshire, a subcontractor or supplier without a contract with the owner should give the owner written notice that it will claim a lien before it performs the labor or furnishes the materials, and then give the owner a written account of labor and materials furnished at least every 30 days while the work continues. A sub that gives notice later generally gets less protection, so check RSA 447:5 to 447:8 for the exact rules.
facts.note: From a law-firm compendium (https://www.alfainternational.com/compendium/construction/new-hampshire/); verify timing rules in RSA 447:5-447:8.
facts.reviewed: Vague on the key timing rule. Under RSA 447:5 a sub or supplier without a contract with the owner protects its full lien by giving the owner written notice before it performs the labor or furnishes the materials; 'must give notice' with no deadline invites a student to send it after the fact. Official RSA pages and Justia could not be loaded to confirm, so status stays unverified.

facts.source: NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, Home Improvement Contractor FAQ; NJ Contractors' Registration Act (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136 et seq.)
facts.fact: New Jersey has no statewide general contractor license exam. Businesses that make or sell home improvements must register annually with the Division of Consumer Affairs as Home Improvement Contractors (HIC), including out-of-state and part-time contractors. New home construction is not a home improvement, and builders registered with the Department of Community Affairs are exempt from HIC registration.
facts.note: https://njconsumeraffairs.gov/hic/Pages/FAQ.aspx

facts.source: NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, HIC FAQ; NJ Business Action Center HIC quick-start guide
facts.fact: New Jersey home improvement contractors must carry commercial general liability insurance of at least $500,000 per occurrence plus workers' compensation unless exempt. Registration must be renewed by March 31 each year, and home improvement contracts over $500 must be in writing.
facts.note: https://njconsumeraffairs.gov/hic/Pages/FAQ.aspx ; https://www.nj.gov/state/bac/assets/pdf/quick-start/home-improvement-contractor.pdf

facts.source: NJ Department of Community Affairs, Builder Registration and New Home Warranty for Builders; New Home Warranty and Builders' Registration Act (N.J.S.A. 46:3B-1 et seq.)
facts.fact: All builders of owner-occupied new homes in New Jersey must register with the DCA New Home Warranty Program, and registration lasts two years from approval. Homes must carry the statutory warranty: broad coverage in year 1, mechanical, electrical, plumbing and major structural defects through year 2, and major structural defects only in years 3 through 10.
facts.note: https://www.nj.gov/dca/divisions/codes/offices/nhw_for_builders.html

facts.source: N.J.S.A. 45:5A-9 (text via Justia); NJ Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors
facts.fact: New Jersey licenses electrical contractors through the Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors. An applicant needs at least five years in electrical construction, including four years in a U.S. Department of Labor-approved apprenticeship and one year as a Class A journeyman, and must pass the electrical contractor exam (with a six-month wait before a retake).
facts.note: Statute text read on Justia (https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-45/section-45-5a-9/); the board's njconsumeraffairs.gov pages would not load to confirm.
keywords: Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors

facts.source: N.J.S.A. 45:14C-15 (text via Justia); NJ State Board of Master Plumbers
facts.fact: New Jersey's State Board of Master Plumbers licenses master plumbers. An applicant must be at least 21 with five years in the plumbing trade, including four years in a DOL-accredited apprenticeship and one year as a journeyman, or hold an accredited bachelor's degree in mechanical, plumbing or sanitary engineering plus one year of practical work, and must pass the exam.
facts.note: Statute text read on Justia (https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-45/section-45-14c-15/); the board site would not load to confirm.

facts.source: NJ State Board of Examiners of Master HVACR Contractors (N.J.S.A. 45:16A-1 et seq.)
facts.fact: New Jersey licenses master HVACR contractors through the State Board of Examiners of Master HVACR Contractors, and HVACR contracting work must be done under a licensed master HVACR contractor.
facts.note: Board existence is well established, but its njconsumeraffairs.gov page would not load in this session to confirm scope and requirements.

facts.source: NJ Construction Lien Law, N.J.S.A. 2A:44A-6 and 2A:44A-21 (text via Justia, 2025)
facts.fact: Under the New Jersey Construction Lien Law, a lien claim on non-residential work must be lodged within 90 days after the claimant last provided work, services, materials or equipment. On residential construction, the claimant must first file a Notice of Unpaid Balance and Right to File Lien and go through arbitration, then lodge the lien within 10 days after the arbitrator's decision and within 120 days after last providing work or materials.
facts.note: Statute text read on Justia (https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-2a/section-2a-44a-6/ and .../section-2a-44a-20/). The residential Notice of Unpaid Balance filing deadline (60 days in the statutory form) should be confirmed in 2A:44A-20/21.

facts.fact: A New Jersey lien claimant must file suit in Superior Court to enforce the lien within one year after last providing work or materials. If the owner or contractor serves written notice demanding suit, the claimant has only 30 days after receiving that notice.
facts.note: Statute text read on Justia (https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-2a/section-2a-44a-14/); the official NJ statute site was not checked.

facts.source: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department, Construction Industries Division (CID); Construction Industries Licensing Act (NMSA 60-13); 14.6.3 NMAC
facts.fact: New Mexico licenses contractors statewide through the Construction Industries Division (CID) of the Regulation and Licensing Department. Each license must have a qualifying party who holds a qualifying party certificate in the license classification (for example general building, electrical, or mechanical).
facts.note: https://www.rld.nm.gov/construction-industries/ ; https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.006.0003.html

facts.fact: A New Mexico qualifying party applicant must document four years of experience within the 10 years before applying before sitting for the exam. Accredited technical training counts as half a year per year of training, up to half the requirement. The passing score on CID exams is 75%, and a failed exam may be retaken no more than twice in any 30-day period.
facts.note: https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.006.0003.html (classification-specific experience is also set in the Act and Title 14 NMAC)

facts.fact: CID may waive New Mexico's state-specific written trade exam for a qualifying party who passed the NASCLA accredited general construction, electrical, or electrical journeyman exam at the passing score, once all other qualifying party requirements are met.
facts.note: https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.006.0003.html

facts.source: Exam prep provider page (theselfemployed.com); PSI testing for CID
facts.fact: New Mexico qualifying parties take a Business and Law exam through PSI in addition to the trade exam: 50 questions in 130 minutes, 75% to pass, covering licensing, estimating, business and financial management, taxes, labor law, lien law, contracts, risk management, and safety. An approved roughly 16-hour Business and Law course is reported to be accepted in place of the exam.
facts.note: Details come from a course provider (https://www.theselfemployed.com/new-mexico-construction-industries-division-business-and-law-exam/); 14.6.3 NMAC does not mention a business and law exam. Confirm with CID and the PSI New Mexico bulletin.
keywords: New Mexico business and law exam

facts.fact: New Mexico contractors must file a $10,000 bond from a corporate surety authorized in New Mexico when first licensed and again at each renewal. A license can also become invalid for failing to comply with workers' compensation laws.
facts.note: https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title14/14.006.0003.html

facts.source: NM RLD Construction Industries Division, Journeyman Certification; 14.6.4 NMAC
facts.fact: New Mexico certifies journeymen through CID (exams through PSI). The only journeyman classification New Mexico accepts by reciprocity is EE-98J (residential and commercial electrical), which requires 8,000 hours of experience, and it is accepted from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nebraska, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, and Wyoming.
facts.note: https://www.rld.nm.gov/construction-industries/ (rule changes to 14.6.4 and 14.6.6 NMAC were pending a 2026 hearing)

facts.fact: In New Mexico, an original contractor must file its claim of lien within 120 days after completing its contract, and everyone else must file within 90 days after the building or improvement is completed. A lien expires two years after it is filed unless enforcement proceedings are started in court or binding arbitration within that time.
facts.note: Statute text read on Justia (https://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-48/article-2/section-48-2-6/ and .../section-48-2-10/); the official NMOneSource text was not checked.

facts.fact: In New Mexico, a lien claimant owed more than $5,000 who did not contract directly with the owner or the original contractor (for example a sub-subcontractor or a supplier to a subcontractor) must send written preliminary notice to the owner or the original contractor within 60 days after first furnishing work or materials. A late notice covers only work furnished from 30 days before it was given. The rule does not apply to original contractors, to subcontractors and suppliers who contracted directly with the original contractor, or to residential property with four or fewer units.
facts.note: Statute text (2025 code) via Justia: https://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-48/article-2/section-48-2-2-1/ ; confirm in the official NMOneSource text.
facts.reviewed: Overstated: the fact said every subcontractor or supplier owed over $5,000 must send notice, but NMSA 48-2-2.1 (2025 code via Justia) also exempts subcontractors and suppliers who contracted directly with the original contractor. The notice duty falls on lower-tier claimants only.

facts.source: Secondary licensing guides; NYC DCWP and DOB licensing pages
facts.fact: New York State has no statewide general contractor license and no statewide electrician or plumber license. Contractor and trade licensing is done locally, for example by New York City, Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester, and Rockland counties, and by individual cities.
facts.note: No official state page stating this was found; based on secondary sources and on the existence of city and county licensing programs. Confirm with the local jurisdiction.

facts.fact: Under New York General Business Law Article 36-A, a home improvement contract worth $500 or more (one or more contracts combined, including labor and materials) must be in writing and signed by all parties, with a signed copy given to the owner before work starts. It must include start and completion dates, a progress payment schedule tied to stages of work, a mechanic's lien notice, a notice about depositing advance payments under the Lien Law (or posting a bond), and the owner's right to cancel until midnight of the third business day.
facts.note: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/770 ; https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/771

facts.source: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), Home Improvement Contractor license checklist
facts.fact: Anyone doing residential home improvement work in New York City needs a Home Improvement Contractor license from the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection. One qualifying person must pass a 30-question exam with at least 21 correct, and the business must enroll in the Home Improvement Business Trust Fund or post a $20,000 surety bond. Licenses last 2 years and expire February 28 of odd-numbered years.
facts.note: https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/businesses/license-checklist-home-improvement-contractor.page

facts.source: NYC DCWP Home Improvement Contractor license checklist
facts.fact: NYC home improvement contractor applicants must provide a New York State workers' compensation insurance certificate naming DCWP as certificate holder, or a Workers' Compensation Board exemption attestation; ACORD forms are not accepted as proof. Owners, officers, and shareholders owning more than 10% must be fingerprinted.
facts.note: https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/businesses/license-checklist-home-improvement-contractor.page

facts.source: NYC Department of Buildings, General Contractor Registration
facts.fact: New York City's Department of Buildings requires general contractors who build one-, two-, and three-family homes under New Building permits to register with the Department. Registration lasts three years.
facts.note: https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/general-contractor-registration.page (insurance amounts are on a separate DOB page that was not reviewed)

facts.source: NYC Department of Buildings licensing (pages not reachable)
facts.fact: In New York City, the Department of Buildings licenses master electricians and master plumbers. Each license requires years of documented experience under a licensed master plus written and practical exams, and only licensed masters may pull permits for electrical or plumbing work in the city.
facts.note: NYC DOB master electrician and master plumber pages would not load in this session; experience-year requirements were left out on purpose and should be confirmed with DOB.

facts.fact: A New York mechanic's lien notice must be filed with the county clerk within eight months after completion of the contract, or within four months for improvements to a single-family dwelling, and may be filed while work is still in progress. The lienor must serve a copy on the owner from five days before to thirty days after filing.
facts.note: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/LIE/10 ; https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/LIE/11

facts.fact: A New York mechanic's lien lasts one year after the notice is filed unless a foreclosure action is started or the lien is extended. Most liens can be extended once for one more year by filing with the county clerk, but liens on single-family dwellings can only be extended by court order (up to one year at a time).
facts.note: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/LIE/17

facts.source: N.C.G.S. 87-1; North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors (NCLBGC)
facts.fact: North Carolina requires a general contractor license from the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors for anyone who, for pay, bids on or builds a building, highway, utility, grading project, or other improvement costing $40,000 or more. Erecting a North Carolina-labeled modular building requires a license regardless of cost.
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_87/GS_87-1.html

facts.fact: North Carolina GC licenses come in three limitations: Limited (single projects up to $750,000), Intermediate (up to $1,500,000), and Unlimited (any value), with land costs excluded. Classifications are building, residential, highway, public utilities (with subclassifications), and specialty.
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_87/GS_87-10.html

facts.source: 21 NCAC 12 .0204 (as amended eff. April 1, 2018, per Rules Review Commission filing)
facts.fact: North Carolina GC applicants must prove financial responsibility through working capital or a surety bond. The 2018 rule set minimum working capital of $17,000 (or $80,000 net worth) for Limited, $75,000 for Intermediate, and $150,000 for Unlimited, or alternatively a surety bond of $350,000, $1,000,000, or $2,000,000 respectively.
facts.note: Figures are from the 2018 rule filing (https://www.oah.nc.gov/documents/rules/rrc/43160-follow-tab-c-general-contractors/open). The statute's project limits have since been raised, so these amounts may have changed; check the current 21 NCAC 12 .0204.

facts.source: N.C.G.S. 87-10(b); PSI North Carolina General Contractor bulletin (updated 11/19/2025)
facts.fact: North Carolina GC qualifiers must pass a Board-approved exam covering plans and specifications, the NC State Building Code, estimating, construction, ethics, NC contractor and lien laws, and the Sedimentation Pollution Control Act. PSI's Building Contractor exam is open book with 90 questions in 200 minutes and a 70% passing score. References include the Contractor's Guide to Business, Law and Project Management (NC General Contractors Edition, 10th), the NC State Building Code, and NC OSHA construction standards.
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_87/GS_87-10.html ; https://test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/454 (the bulletin lists 2018 NC code editions, so check for updates)

facts.fact: Each year, at least one qualifier of a North Carolina licensee with a building, residential, or unclassified classification must complete 8 hours of approved continuing education. Two of those hours must be the Board's mandatory course and six may be electives, and a licensee can choose inactive status instead.
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_87/GS_87-10.2.html

facts.source: N.C.G.S. 87-43.3; North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors
facts.fact: The North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors licenses electrical contractors in Limited (single projects up to a Board-set value not over $100,000, equipment rated 1,000 volts or less), Intermediate (Board-set value not over $200,000), and Unlimited (any value) classes, plus special restricted classes for limited phases of electrical work.
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_87/GS_87-43.3.html (the Board sets the actual project limits within these statutory caps)
keywords: Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors

facts.source: N.C.G.S. 87-21; North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating, and Fire Sprinkler Contractors
facts.fact: North Carolina's State Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating, and Fire Sprinkler Contractors licenses plumbing, heating, and fire sprinkler contractors. A Class I license covers all structures, and a Class II license covers plumbing and heating in single-family detached homes only. Heating is split into group one (steam and hot water), group two (air systems over 15 tons of refrigeration capacity), and group three (systems of 15 tons or less, including all single-family residential systems).
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_87/GS_87-21.html

facts.fact: For North Carolina improvements costing $40,000 or more, the owner must designate a lien agent; improvements to an existing owner-occupied single-family home are exempt. Potential lien claimants must send a Notice to Lien Agent within 15 days after first furnishing labor or materials, or risk losing lien rights against later purchasers and priority over recorded mortgages.
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_44A/GS_44A-11.1.html ; https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_44A/GS_44A-11.2.html

facts.fact: A North Carolina claim of lien on real property must be filed no later than 120 days after the claimant last furnished labor or materials to the site. A lawsuit to enforce the lien must be filed no later than 180 days after that last furnishing.
facts.note: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_44A/GS_44A-12.html ; https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_44A/GS_44A-13.html

facts.source: N.D.C.C. 43-07-02 and 43-07-07; North Dakota Secretary of State (contractor registrar)
facts.fact: North Dakota requires a contractor license from the Secretary of State (the registrar) whenever the cost, value, or price per job exceeds $4,000. Licenses come in four classes by largest single project: Class A has no limit, Class B allows up to $500,000, Class C up to $300,000, and Class D up to $100,000.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c07.pdf

facts.fact: A North Dakota contractor license application must include a certificate of liability insurance naming the registrar (Secretary of State) as certificate holder. The statute does not set coverage amounts in that section.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c07.pdf ; workers' compensation coverage through ND WSI is also generally required but was not confirmed in this session

facts.fact: North Dakota contractor licenses run on a contractor year from March 2 through March 1 and must be renewed before March 2 each year. A contractor who misses that date has until June 1 to renew by paying a late penalty.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c07.pdf

facts.source: N.D.C.C. 43-09-10, 43-09-11, 43-09-20; North Dakota State Electrical Board
facts.fact: The North Dakota State Electrical Board licenses master, journeyman, class B, and power limited electricians. A journeyman needs 8,000 hours of wiring experience over at least three years (plus approved apprenticeship training or a two-year program for apprentices registered after January 31, 2008), and a master needs one year as a licensed journeyman. Only master and power limited electricians may enter electrical installation contracts, with a narrow class B exception.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c09.pdf

facts.fact: North Dakota electrical licenses are issued for one year and renew annually without re-examination. Licensees must complete at least 8 hours of continuing education each two-year biennium, and the board may not require more than 16 hours.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c09.pdf

facts.source: N.D.C.C. ch. 43-18; North Dakota State Board of Plumbing
facts.fact: The North Dakota State Board of Plumbing licenses master and journeyman plumbers and registers apprentices, with qualifications set by board rule. Licenses expire December 31 of the year issued, and renewal requires plumbing continuing education of at least 2 credit hours (the board may require up to 4) within each two-year period.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c18.pdf (experience requirements are in the board's administrative rules, not checked)
facts.reviewed: N.D.C.C. 43-18-17.1 sets plumbing CE at a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4 credit hours within a two-year period; the fact implied 2 hours per (annual) renewal.

facts.fact: A North Dakota construction lien claimant must send the owner written notice of intent to claim a lien by certified mail at least 10 days before recording the lien. The lien should be recorded within 90 days after the claimant's work is done; a later filing is still allowed but does not bind good-faith purchasers or lenders whose rights arose before it, and no lien may be filed more than three years after the first materials were furnished.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t35c27.pdf

facts.fact: Before suing to enforce a North Dakota construction lien, the lienholder must give notice at least 10 days ahead by personal service or 20 days ahead by registered mail. The suit and a lis pendens must be filed within three years after the lien is recorded, or within 30 days after the owner delivers a written demand, or the lien is lost.
facts.note: https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t35c27.pdf
